title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 13
statement:
How many nonnegative integers can be written in the form

\[ \begin{aligned} &a_7 \cdot 3^7 + a_6 \cdot 3^6 + a_5 \cdot 3^5 \\ &\quad {}+ a_4 \cdot 3^4 + a_3 \cdot 3^3 + a_2 \cdot 3^2 \\ &\quad {}+ a_1 \cdot 3^1 + a_0 \cdot 3^0, \end{aligned} \]

where \(a_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}\) for \(0 \le i \le 7?\)

solutions.text:
Adding \(1\) to every \(a_i\) gives a bijection between these expressions and the base-\(3\) numerals for \(0\) through \(3^8 - 1,\) so exactly \(3^8 = 6561\) distinct integers occur. They are symmetric about \(0\) (negating all \(a_i\) negates the value), so besides \(0\) itself, half are positive: \[ 1 + \tfrac12(6561 - 1) = 3281 \] nonnegative integers, namely \(0\) through \(3280.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Shifting each \(a_i\) from \(\{-1, 0, 1\}\) to \(\{0, 1, 2\}\) makes an ordinary base-\(3\) numeral
The \(3^8\) representable integers are symmetric about \(0;\) count \(0\) together with half of the remaining values
